title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Ops Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This page defines the standards, templates, operating procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, the docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues we see in the field with canonical remediation steps. The goal is to provide a single, prescriptive reference so docs are discoverable, consistent, and low-maintenance.

Goals

- Provide consistent, production-ready developer docs that reduce onboarding time and support load.
- Ensure examples reflect current SDKs and API surface (language parity, streaming, function calls).
- Lower time-to-resolution for common support cases by documenting canonical fixes.
- Maintain a lightweight operating process so docs stay accurate as SDKs and runtime behavior evolve.

Scope

This playbook applies to all public-facing DevEx artifacts under the eng-developer-experience space, including:
- SDK Guides (Python, Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and Templates (starter apps, terraform examples)
- API Examples (curl, JSON payloads, streaming examples)
- Docs site operating procedures (release cadence, versioning, redirects)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage + remediation steps)

Ownership and SLAs

| Component | Primary Owner | Review cadence | SLO for critical fixes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SDK Guides | DevEx (docs-engineering) | every 6 months or on SDK release | 48 hours for P1 fixes |
| Quickstarts & Templates | DevEx + Solutions Eng | every 3 months | 72 hours |
| API Examples | API Owner + DevEx | on API change | 24 hours for regressions caused by API changes |
| Docs site ops | DevEx + Infra | quarterly | 7 days for critical site outages |

Note: Primary owner is responsible for review, merge approvals, and tagging reviewers. SLAs apply to published docs that are used by customers or internal teams.

Doc Types and Templates (must use these)

All new docs in this space must start from the canonical templates stored in the quickstarts-and-templates directory. Mandatory sections by doc type:

1) SDK Guide template
- Title, short intro (1–2 paragraphs)
- Quick example (copy-paste runnable)
- Detailed API reference (table of main methods + inputs/outputs)
- Configuration and auth (environment variables, token scopes)
- Error handling & retries (common error codes, backoff examples)
- Troubleshooting (top 5 issues)
- Changelog & compatibility notes

2) Quickstart/Template template
- Goal & what you will build
- Pre-reqs (account, CLI, environment)
- Step-by-step numbered instructions with expected output
- Deployment checklist (secrets, IAM, billing)
- Minimal working code in repo style
- Test/verify steps and smoke tests

3) API Example page
- Purpose & where to use (curl vs SDK)
- Simple sync request example (curl + JSON)
- Streaming example (client code + server expectations)
- Function/tool calling example (if applicable)
- Response schema examples and notes on error flux

Minimum formatting rules

- Use short descriptive file names with dashes and year (see directory naming convention).
- Include a one-line summary at the top and a 1–2 sentence intro.
- Use numbered steps for procedures and bullets for lists.
- Include runnable examples (copy/paste) for at least one SDK and curl.
- All code snippets must include the exact SDK version used and a pinned package reference (e.g., pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.2).

SDK Guides (examples)

Minimal Python quick example (must be present near the top of each SDK guide):

```python
# pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.2
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.generate(text="Write a 3-line haiku about caching.")
print(resp.text)
```

Minimal Node.js quick example:

```javascript
// npm install @redwood/inference@1.4.2
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ prompt: 'Summarize the benefits of batching.' });
console.log(resp.text);
```

Authentication & config table

| Variable | Purpose | Recommended scope | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | API authentication | read+generate (default) | sk-prod-xxxx |
| REDWOOD_REGION | Region selection for routing | eu-west-1, us-east-1 | us-east-1 |
| REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS | SDK request timeout override | 30000 | 30000 |

Quickstarts and Templates

Canonical quickstarts must include a repo-level README with a one-command start and a minimal CI job that runs smoke tests. Templates we maintain: 
- simple-chatbot-starter (Python FastAPI + streaming)
- batch-embeddings-pipeline (Go worker + Postgres)
- reranker-demo (Node.js + sample dataset)
- terraform-dedicated-deploy (reference infra for Dedicated)

Each template must include a TEST.md with clear verification steps and expected outputs (e.g., expected latency < 500ms for local inference with quantized model).

API Examples

Guidance: Always provide both curl and at least one SDK example for any API surface that customers use. When demonstrating streaming, show a minimal client that consumes chunks and a short note on reconnect behavior.

Curl generate example:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0", "input":"Explain continuous batching in 2 sentences."}'

Streaming note:
- For long-running responses use the SDK streaming methods to preserve incremental tokens and reduce memory.
- Document how to rehydrate from last-known sequence id after transient disconnects.

Docs Site Operating Procedures

Release cadence
1. Minor docs fixes: merged to main and deployed automatically (CI deploy) — no scheduled approval required unless they touch API surfaces.
2. Major changes (SDK or API breaking): create docs PR with CHANGELOG entry, link to release PR, tag reviewers from API and DevEx teams. Coordinate with Release Manager.
3. Quarterly review: owners must confirm correctness or mark as deprecated.

Versioning and redirects
- All published examples should include a pinned SDK version.
- When deprecating an example, add a redirect and keep a compatibility note for 12 months.

Content freeze and hotfixes
- Freeze content for 48 hours around major product launches. Hotfix process: create a P0 docs PR and notify #doc-updates. Owner must merge within SLA.

Editorial checklist (pre-publish)
- Run the docs linter (scripts/docs-lint.sh)
- Smoke test examples locally (scripts/smoke-test.sh)
- Add/update CHANGELOG and compatibility matrix
- Add labels and related_pages metadata

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes

We track top issues from support tickets and include canonical fixes that documentation authors must add to their troubleshooting section. Below are the top recurring problems as of last review and the canonical remediation steps.

1) Auth failures from local devs (most common)
- Symptom: 401 / "invalid_api_key" on curl or SDK call.
- Root cause: using expired or environment-scoped key, or inadvertently setting REDWOOD_API_KEY in CI with a read-only token.
- Canonical fix to document: 1) Run `redwood keys create --scope=read+generate --name=dev-local` and copy key into local env. 2) Verify with `curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`. 3) Add troubleshooting note and sample error output to SDK guides.

2) Streaming disconnects during long responses
- Symptom: partial data returned, client reconnects and receives duplicate prefix.
- Root cause: transient network or client-side timeout.
- Canonical fix to document: implement idempotent rehydration using last_token_index in SDK (example snippet below). Include recommended client-side backoff: exponential backoff with jitter (base 200ms, max 5s).

3) Mismatched model variant kills (latency regressions)
- Symptom: previously fast endpoint shows 3–5x latency increase.
- Root cause: traffic routed to higher-precision model variant during rollout.
- Canonical fix to document: check route policy in Console (Route -> Model Variant), pin model variant in SDK request (model_variant: "redwood-1.0-int8"), add note on how to contact infra for emergency rollback.

4) Embedding batch size OOM in customers' workers
- Symptom: OOM during large batch embedding job.
- Root cause: client-side batching larger than recommended, or wrong tensor dtype in client binding.
- Canonical fix to document: recommend batch size <= 512 for t4/gbp-16 profiles, provide retry pattern: chunk input, use concurrency limiters, and sample code for streaming embeddings.

Publishing and Review Workflow

1. Author creates a docs PR using the canonical template.
2. Assign reviewers: at least one DevEx reviewer + one API owner for API-level content.
3. Run CI checks: lint, smoke tests, link checks.
4. Merge after approvals; minor content is auto-deployed.

Escalation matrix for broken/incorrect examples
- P0 (customer-facing regression): Notify #doc-updates and #support, page owner and API owner must triage within 2 hours.
- P1 (internal docs or low-impact): Owner triages within SLA defined above.

Appendix: Template Checklist (required on PR description)
- [ ] Uses canonical template from quickstarts-and-templates
- [ ] Includes runnable quick example for latest SDK version
- [ ] Includes troubleshooting with at least 3 items
- [ ] Has reviewers assigned and labels set
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry created

Contact

If you are updating a doc and are unsure whether it fits these standards, ping the DevEx team on Slack or open a draft PR and request review.
